answer.answer:
Prefabrication has two hard requirements of its own: precise up-front planning and logistics, and a regulatory route, meaning third-party certification and traceability so that factory-made work can be shown to comply. It is brought into a project by three upstream moves: designing for manufacture and assembly, bringing the fabricator or contractor into the early design phase, and integrating the supply chain. What it returns is schedule compression, better quality, fewer errors and rework, and safer sites, all of it resting on peer-reviewed literature rather than on any deployed Japanese case in the material here, and note that only the graph's own relation labels, not the words of the question, license these readings.

**What prefabrication requires**

Prefabrication/off-site (PR2) carries exactly 4 inbound and 6 outbound dependency edges, and all ten are listed in the context, so the following is complete for this enabler.

Two of its outbound edges are requirements:

- PR2 depends on Rely on precise planning (RI14): prefabrication relies on precise up-front planning and logistics [1], on peer-reviewed evidence [1]. RI14 is itself widely present, activated in 36 of the 50 coded cases.
- PR2 depends on Regulatory/legal concern (RI18): a functional regulatory system for offsite compliance requires third-party certification and traceability [2], again peer-reviewed [2]. RI18 is a shared chokepoint: it carries 5 inbound dependency edges and none outbound, the other four being human-robot collaborative work (CO6), robot technology design and integration (AT3), and printed concrete walls and on-site printing (PR3, PR8), which are gated by robot safety standards and by printing acceptance criteria respectively.

**What brings prefabrication about**

Three of the four inbound edges point at PR2 as a capability to be enabled:

- DfMA for DFAB process (PR9) enables PR2: DfMA orients the project toward offsite manufacture [3] (peer-reviewed).
- Early contractor involvement (CO11) enables PR2: integrating manufacturing and assembly knowledge into design requires the delivering production party, manufacturer, fabricator or contractor, to be involved in the early design phase, and a delivery method that involves participants in early design should be selected [4] (peer-reviewed).
- Supply chain integration (VA14) enables PR2: supply chain integration supports the offsite production line [5] (peer-reviewed).

The fourth inbound edge runs the other way in substance: automated overhead delivery and assembly (PR4) has prefabrication as a precondition, since it requires extensive prefabrication and unification of materials [5]. That is PR4 depending on PR2, not a dependency of prefabrication.

**What it yields**

The remaining four outbound edges are all enablements, all peer-reviewed: reduce time and improve productivity (VA2), since offsite factory work compresses schedule [6]; improve quality and performance (VA3) through the controlled factory environment [7]; reduce errors and constraints (VA10), since factory-based production improves quality control and reduces errors and rework [8]; and improve site safety (VA13), by moving work offsite [9]. Site safety has exactly one inbound dependency edge in the graph, this one, so prefabrication is the single cited route to it at present.

**Weight in the coded record**

PR2 is activated in 20 of the 50 coded cases. Of its neighbours, VA2 is activated in 49, VA3 in 37, VA13 in 39, VA10 in 19, RI14 in 36, RI18 in 12, PR9 in 15 and CO11 in 14. The gap between the near-universal outcomes and the far narrower presence of DfMA and early contractor involvement is worth noting: the benefits are claimed much more often than the two organisational moves that the literature says produce them.

**Limits of this evidence**

Every edge above is literature-based, either peer-reviewed or, for the standards layer around RI18, standard-grade. No Process RP record and no CensusProcess record appears in the context for prefabrication, and no firm is named, so nothing here rests on a deployed Japanese line; I cannot point you at a coded case for PR2 from what is in front of me. The co-occurrence figures shown, for instance the 49-case pairing of digital design tools with productivity, are statistical associations across cases and do not assert direction.
